newsitem.title: USA: Dow off at midday, high techs rally.
newsitem.headline: Dow off at midday, high techs rally.

text.p: The Dow Industrials were down at midday on Inauguration day in the United States, but an earnings-driven rally in Microsoft Corp led the high techs and Nasdaq higher.

The Dow was down 10 points at 6822 while declines led advancing issues by 12 to 10 on volume of about 207 million shares. Nasdaq was up 10 at 1359. The bond market was closed in observance of Martin Luther King Jr Day.
"We are having a Nasdaq day," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
"The Microsoft numbers were strong. There is a follow through of upward momentum on Nasdaq, and it has been outperforming the other averages all day," Bleier said.

Microsoft, the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, was up 3-3/8 at 90-1/2. Microsoft warned about slower earnings growth in 1998, but the market took it in stride. "They always issue a warning but remain the undisputed software champ," Bleier said. Other high techs followed, with Intel up 1-13/16 at 145-7/8, Cisco Systems Inc up 2-1/16 at 74-11/16, U.S. Robotics Corp up 2-1/4 at 73-7/8 and Ascend Communications Inc up 2-1/2 at 77-1/2.

Elsewhere in the market, shares of First USA Inc rallied 8-5/8 to 45-3/8 on its agreement to be acquired by Banc One Corp for $7.3 billion in stock, or about $52.61 per share. Banc One was down 3-3/4 at 41-3/8.
Shares of "monoline" credit card issuers also rose. Advanta Corp was up 4-3/8 at 47-1/2. MBNA Corp was up 1-3/4 at 32-7/8 and Capital One Financial Corp rose 4-1/4 to 37-3/4.
But Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp, said that while the sector would benefit, the merger had little effect on the overall market.
"What helps stocks, in my view, is when one company buys another for cash. That means there is a flow of money into the stock market," Johnson said.
"In this case Banc One is buying First USA for stock so that while it is a big and interesting deal, it does not in my mind improve where the overall stock market is heading."
Johnson said that today's early Dow pullback was to be expected after the strong run the average had this year.
"There is some edginess, nervousness no matter how good things are. We can't maintain this clip," he said.
Nasdaq said Monday that it had begun trading under new order handling rules intended to reduce the minimum number of shares that dealers can quote when they are not displaying customer limit orders.
The minimum limit order quote size has now been cut to 100 from the previous 1,000 shares. It will be applied on a pilot basis on the 50 most active stocks traded on Nasdaq.
The New York Stock Exchange said it stopped trading for one minute at 1200 EST/1700 GMT in observance of the birthday of slain civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr, a federal holiday.
